# Work with local Joplin notes

1. Run `python3 joplin_notes.py` from this skill directory with a subcommand below (Python 3.9+). Reads open SQLite in read-only mode. The default is `~/.config/joplin/database.sqlite`, with `~/.config/joplin-desktop/database.sqlite` as the read fallback. To select a profile, put `--db PATH` or `--profile DIR` before the subcommand. Either overrides `JOPLIN_DB`. Synced notes are stored locally in decrypted form after Joplin decrypts them. Leave sync E2EE enabled.
2. Choose a read command. Results exclude trashed and conflict notes. Put `--include-conflicts` before the subcommand to include available conflicts. Joplin omits conflicts from its full-text index, so use `grep` to find them or recently written text awaiting indexing. Notebook selectors accept a full ID, a path or a unique title.

   | Subcommand | Result |
   | --- | --- |
   | `notebooks` | Notebook path, direct note count and ID |
   | `search "meeting minutes"` | Full-text matches with ID, notebook, title and UTC update time. Title hits count triple and newer notes break ties. |
   | `grep -i "action items?"` | Matching title and body lines with ID, title and line number (the title is line 1) |
   | `show "Meeting minutes"` | Title, notebook, tags, timestamps and Markdown. Use a full note ID for duplicate titles. |
   | `recent -n 5 --notebook "Work/Planning"` | Most recently updated notes in that notebook. Omit the filter for all notebooks. |

3. Write through the terminal CLI with the TUI open. Switch away from the notebook and back to see changes. Its count may stay stale. Finish any external-editor session first because CLI startup removes `edit-*` temporary files. Preview either write with `--dry-run` (the output includes body text).
4. Use `create` with an existing notebook and a UTF-8 Markdown file. The CLI keeps the destination selected.

   ```sh
   python3 joplin_notes.py create --notebook "Work/Planning" --title "Meeting minutes" --body-file minutes.md --tag meeting
   ```

5. Use `update` with the full 32-hex ID from a read command. Choose `--body-file` to replace the Markdown or `--append-file` to add text after a blank line. Append reads and replaces the whole body, so avoid editing that body concurrently. Supply only the changes requested.

   ```sh
   python3 joplin_notes.py update "$note_id" --append-file decisions.md --title "Planning decisions" --tag reviewed --untag draft --notebook "Work/Archive"
   ```

6. Verify with `show` and the returned ID. If a write fails partway, inspect the note or draft before retrying, especially before another append. Use synthetic examples for upstream feedback.
